bounded_conclusions: Production +u/dt is the partial derivative of the affine q_u extension with predictor u and q_bot held fixed.
Along the already-qualified E4 B3 flux-driven predictor family, q_bot changes with H and cancels +u/dt to first order because dq_bot/dH is approximately u/dt.
With baseline u frozen, the total q_u slope is at most about 3.8e-8 of the production partial slope on the fixed E4 plateau points.
Using each predictor point's own u leaves the observed total q_u slope below about 9.8e-7 of the production partial slope.
Therefore production dq_u/dH=+u/dt must not be described as the total derivative of historical q_u across neighboring predictor trajectories.

This distinction does not by itself invalidate the production slope: MAP04 and MAP05A show that an affine iteration-response slope can be a numerical policy while accepted physics is certified by the real corrector and ledger.
synthesis_with_prior_maps: MAP03 identifies u with local whole-column storage sensitivity in the simple drainage-free fixture and bottom-outward exchange sensitivity with -u.
MAP05A shows both current +u and independently measured negative J_R can converge to equivalent accepted B3 physics.
MAP06 shows slope policy matters for path robustness because the B3 corrector admissibility set is deterministic but fragmented.
forbidden_inference: Do not relabel +u/dt as a physical interface-exchange Jacobian.
Do not call the partial-versus-total distinction a production defect without an explicit coupling-contract requirement.
Do not replace production u_A by J_R from this diagnostic.
